original_question: Let G be a connected graph on n vertices with minimum degree delta, and let mu_1 >= ... >= mu_n be the Laplacian eigenvalues. Must the toughness satisfy t(G) >= mu_{n-1}/(mu_1 - delta)?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Conjecture 8 (Haemers) of arXiv:2305.10290, which restates the toughness-from-Laplacian conjecture; the cited source is Gu–Haemers, Section 2, Conjecture 2.1 in Graph toughness from Laplacian eigenvalues.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target: the exact conjectural lower bound on graph toughness in terms of the Laplacian eigenvalues and the minimum degree, for connected graphs, using the survey's decreasing Laplacian ordering (so μ_{n-1} is the algebraic connectivity and μ_1 is the Laplacian spectral radius). It also keeps the scope narrow and does not drift to the neighboring Hamiltonicity conjecture or to the weaker supporting bounds.
missing_details: State that G is a simple, undirected, unweighted graph.
Define the Laplacian matrix explicitly as L(G)=D(G)-A(G).
State the eigenvalue ordering explicitly: μ_1(G) ≥ μ_2(G) ≥ ... ≥ μ_n(G)=0.
Define c(G-S) as the number of connected components of G-S.
Define toughness explicitly: t(G)=min{|S|/c(G-S) : S ⊊ V(G), c(G-S)>1}.
Include the standard convention t(K_n)=∞ to make the question fully stand-alone.
Make the universal quantifier explicit: the question asks whether every connected graph G on n vertices with minimum degree δ satisfies the inequality.
refined_question: Let G=(V,E) be a simple connected graph on n vertices, let δ=δ(G) be its minimum degree, and let L(G)=D(G)-A(G) be its Laplacian matrix with eigenvalues ordered as μ_1(G) ≥ μ_2(G) ≥ ... ≥ μ_n(G)=0. Writing c(H) for the number of connected components of a graph H, and defining the toughness of G by t(G)=min{|S|/c(G-S) : S ⊊ V(G), c(G-S)>1} (with the convention t(K_n)=∞), is it true that every such graph satisfies t(G) ≥ μ_{n-1}(G)/(μ_1(G)-δ)?
justification: The draft is aimed exactly at the survey's Section 7, Conjecture 8, where Liu and Ning state Haemers's conjecture in decreasing Laplacian order as t(G) ≥ μ_{n-1}/(μ_1-δ) for connected graphs. The same nearby passage defines toughness, notes that the conjecture is stronger than Brouwer's conjecture in the regular case, and records four verified cases, so the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should stay with this exact inequality rather than broadening to other spectral toughness bounds or to the later Hamiltonicity discussion. The underlying source is Gu–Haemers, where the same conjecture appears in the paper Graph toughness from Laplacian eigenvalues together with the two supporting lower bounds and the four special cases. No ambient field, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' quantifier issues arise here; the missing pieces are only the graph-theoretic definitions and conventions needed to make the question self-contained.
